figures.caption: Model architecture and two-stage training of Spatial-UMI-Dream. In both stages, dual-gripper RGB and metric depth (Fig. 3) form a unified RGB-D canvas. The Wan VAE encodes observation history and current RGB-D inputs into visual tokens, while a text encoder supplies language tokens through cross-attention. The shared world-action transformer uses block-causal attention to condition prediction on preceding visual history. Stage 1: world-only adaptation predicts future RGB-D observations, decoded through the Wan VAE and supervised by $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{world}}$. Joint world-action training additionally encodes UMI state and noisy actions, and jointly predicts future RGB-D observations and actions through the Wan VAE and action decoder, optimized with $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{world}}+\lambda_{a}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}$.

abstract: The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) enables scalable demonstration collection independently of a specific robot. However, its moving, close-range gripper cameras entangle camera and object motion without a stable external view, leaving the metric geometry needed for precise manipulation implicit in RGB. We introduce Spatial-UMI-Dream, a 5B spatial World Action Model (WAM) pretrained on 605 hours of RGB-D UMI data through two-stage training—world-only adaptation followed by joint world-action learning—to jointly predict future RGB, fisheye-aligned metric depth, and actions. Stereo-derived depth makes scene scale and spatial relationships explicit within a unified dual-gripper RGB-D representation. Furthermore, evaluating UMI policies requires testing whether UMI’s robot-independent demonstration collection translates into policy generalization across robot embodiments, alongside robustness to environmental changes. We introduce RoboTwin-UMI, a twenty-task simulation benchmark built on RoboTwin with UMI wrist-mounted fisheye observations, enabling controlled, repeatable evaluation of UMI policies under environment and embodiment changes separately and jointly without additional fine-tuning. On RoboTwin-UMI, Spatial-UMI-Dream achieves 79.10% in-domain success and 72.15% under combined embodiment and environment shifts, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline in each setting by 4.65 and 10.30 percentage points, respectively. It also exhibits the smallest success-rate drop under embodiment transfer among the evaluated policies. In a matched pretraining ablation, RGB-only pretraining leads to a 5.75-percentage-point decrease in in-domain success compared with RGB-D pretraining. Across six real-world tasks, Spatial-UMI-Dream achieves 85.0% average success, exceeding the strongest baseline by 24.2 percentage points. Our project page is available at https://weiduoyuan.com/spatial-umi-dream/.

sections.body: The paper states that UMI's wrist-mounted fisheye cameras move with the gripper, so image changes mix camera motion, object motion and scene geometry. It proposes Spatial-UMI-Dream, a 5B world action model pretrained on 605 hours of RGB-D UMI data in two stages. Stereo from calibrated cameras provides metric depth aligned with the fisheye RGB. It also introduces RoboTwin-UMI, a twenty-task simulation benchmark that tests environment and embodiment shifts separately and jointly without fine-tuning.
sections.heading: INTRODUCTION
sections.headline: Moving close-range cameras leave scene scale implicit, motivating metric depth and a benchmark that tests embodiment and lighting shifts.

sections.body: Related work groups robot foundation models into action-centric vision-language-action models, world-model methods that do not fully couple world and action generation, and world action models that jointly generate observations and actions. It states that RGB-only world action models leave metric geometry implicit in appearance. Geometry-aware policies either encode depth or point clouds as policy input or distill features from pretrained 3D models into RGB backbones. The paper says its model predicts RGB, registered metric depth and actions jointly, without a separate 3D encoder or alignment teacher.
sections.heading: RELATED WORK
sections.headline: Prior world action models leave geometry implicit, while geometry-aware policies use depth as input or as a distillation target.

sections.body: Each gripper's RGB view is paired with metric depth from stereo: the middle and right cameras are rectified, disparity comes from Fast FoundationStereo, and depth is mapped back to the middle camera's fisheye view. Depth is encoded as three channels with a Turbo colormap over fixed bounds, then stacked with both RGB views into a 320×320 canvas encoded by the pretrained Wan2.2 VAE. The transformer jointly denoises video and action tokens with block-causal attention under a flow-matching objective. Training runs world-only adaptation first, then joint world-action training initialized from it. Handheld demonstrations are filtered by replaying inverse-kinematics motions and dropping episodes above the 99th percentile for velocity, acceleration or jerk. Gripper commands are compensated with a calibrated first-order delay model.
sections.heading: METHOD
sections.headline: A 5B model jointly predicts RGB-D canvases and actions, trained in two stages on filtered, delay-compensated demonstrations.

sections.body: On six real-world bimanual tasks, the model reaches 85.0% average success, against 60.8% for the strongest baseline. On the twenty-task RoboTwin-UMI benchmark, in-domain success is 79.10%, which is 4.65 percentage points above the strongest VLA baseline at 74.45%. Under combined embodiment and lighting shifts, success is 72.15%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 10.30 percentage points. Each setting runs 100 episodes per task, averaged over the twenty tasks. In a matched ablation, RGB-only pretraining lowers in-domain success by 5.75 percentage points compared with RGB-D pretraining. The text also reports that the gap to the strongest baseline widens to 14.00 percentage points after embodiment transfer.
sections.heading: EXPERIMENTS
sections.headline: Spatial-UMI-Dream reaches 79.10% in-domain and 72.15% under joint shifts, with 85.0% average success on six real-world tasks.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the two contributions: the 5B spatial world action model trained on 605 hours of UMI data, and the RoboTwin-UMI benchmark for controlled evaluation across embodiments and environment changes. It reports 85.0% mean success on six real-world tasks and the highest success rates across all benchmark settings. It attributes the benefit of explicit metric geometry to the matched RGB-only ablation. It also cites complementary gains from world-only adaptation and joint world-action learning. The section says these gains extend to precise grasping and placement under moving wrist observations.
sections.heading: CONCLUSION
sections.headline: The conclusion restates that metric geometry and two-stage pretraining drive gains in simulation and on six real-world tasks.

sections.body: The training recipe section gives AdamW with learning rate 10^-5, a cosine schedule, and the stage settings in Table III, including 30k updates with batch size 192 for each pretraining stage. The RoboTwin-UMI setup describes fisheye rendering from four co-centered views at 320×320, with a 92° forward view and 106° auxiliary views. It also describes a joint planner for both arms and the randomized-lighting procedure. Table IV lists the twenty tasks with step limits. Table V lists six real-world tasks with 180 demonstrations and 69,032 frames in total.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists the training recipe, RoboTwin-UMI rendering and planning setup, and the task tables with step limits and scored stages.
